layers._comment: The POIs 口岸模式 is ABOUT. Before this the mode drew only camera dots: three panels of queue and ferry times with nothing on the map saying which crossings they referred to — the panel-to-map link was missing in the one mode where the map should lead. Positions come from data/control_points.json (reference data with a validation trail: each coordinate checked against an official anchor and rejected beyond 1.5km, which caught four wrong lookups). The popup joins the LIVE queue reading from the trigger state, so it answers the panel's question rather than restating the name. 深圳灣 has no coordinate — it is resolved at district level instead of being given a confident wrong pin.

layers._title_note: MEASURED 2026-09-24: an earlier title 停水位置（大廈／街道）＋受影響地區 was 17 characters and the LAYERS control is 230px wide, so it ellipsised mid-word to 停水位置（大廈／街道）＋受… — a layer name the reader could not finish. Now that the district tint is gone the name is simply 停水位置, which fits with room to spare.
layers._comment: Cyrus 2026-09-25: 'boundary polygon 有誤導性; 我覺得顯示 point location 就夠' — so this is now PINS ONLY, and the district TINT is deleted. He is right, and the numbers say why: the tint was a whole 18-district CSDI polygon painted for an outage that is usually ONE building, so 「觀塘區」 went red because of a single 牛頭角道 notice. The pins come from the collector's ALS geocode of each notice's own street address, so they are the actual claim the data supports; the polygon was an inference drawn on top of it and it overstated the affected area every single time. Pins stay two-tone — alert red for 食水 (drinking water, the life-safety case) and amber for 鹹水 (flushing water) — and the layer title no longer mentions districts because it no longer draws any. CONSEQUENCE: the CSDI 18-district source `wsd_water_suspension_districts` and its geometry are now unused, and `polygonLayer`/`normaliseDistricts` were deleted with it. If the tint ever returns, the 深水埗區 trailing-CRLF fix that `normaliseDistricts` existed for is in git history — and it is a real upstream defect, not a rumour.

WIND FLOW — a GPU particle animation over a MODELLED 22x16 lattice (Open-Meteo, 352 points), not the station barbs it used to draw. Cyrus 2026-09-25. The barbs answered 'what is the wind at this instrument'; a flow animation answers 'where is the air going', which is what a reader reads off a weather map. geom is 'none' because zero MapLibre layers are created — map/wind.ts draws the whole thing through a deck.gl MapboxOverlay, so visibility belongs to that overlay, like the 3D layer, and clearVerticalLayers has nothing to clear. It used to be 'poi' with a stale 'wind-barb' symbol, which worked only by accident: 'poi' MEANS the curated border-crossing POI renderer, so listing this layer in a vertical would have handed a modelled wind field to the control-point drawer. HONESTY: this is modelled data; the weather_stations layer is the OBSERVED counterpart and both are one click apart, because conflating a model with a measurement is the dishonest option. Zero MapLibre layers are created, so nothing needs clearing.

The first polygon layer since 2026-09-25. That removal was specific to the water district tint, whose polygon asserted more than the notice said (a district outline around a water suspension reads as the whole district being cut off). Nothing about that reason applies here: CAD publishes the zone AS this boundary, so the polygon IS the data rather than a generalisation of it. OFF by default — 290 polygons at 3MB is not first paint.

4,652 public defibrillators, clustered by the generic point path (clusterRadius 46, clusterMaxZoom 13) exactly like the camera layers — no bespoke clustering code, because the pattern already existed and re-writing it for one layer is how two cluster behaviours end up on one map. OFF by default: it is 707KB, and a layer that loads by default is a layer every reader pays for. The popup answers ONE question first — can the public use it — because an AED behind a locked office door and one on a street corner are the same dot otherwise.

公眾貨物裝卸區 + 機場進場限制區. The facilities 貨運模式's panels are ABOUT: before this the mode listed flight and traffic rows with the map saying nothing about where cargo actually moves, which is the panel-to-map link missing in the one mode where the map should lead. Polygon is right here for the same reason it is right for the drone RFZ and wrong for the water district tint: the publishers draw the zone AS this boundary, so the polygon IS the data rather than a generalisation of it. OFF by default - 128 polygons is 134KB, and a layer that loads unasked is a layer every reader pays for. Popup properties follow the CSDI shape attributeHtml expects (Name as the head, Type_tc/Type_en as a labelled row) - short keys render as '未命名' plus raw unlabelled keys.

23 licensed oil storage installations. A `point` layer must name a `symbol` and pointLayer throws without one (overlays.ts:347); the glyph is `oil-tank` in symbols.ts. Small enough (7,932 bytes) that size is NOT the reason it is off by default — being one mode's subject is: a layer that appears in 總覽 without being asked for is what the verticals exist to prevent.

Live ADS-B traffic. Restored with the same change that restored the panel: the layer was withdrawn because adsb.lol blocks cloud egress, and the map now reads data/aircraft.json published by the PC collector instead of the upstream host. `symbol: plane` plus a per-feature icon-rotate is the existing path in overlays.ts pointLayer — the glyph and the rotation were left intact through the withdrawal, so this is a config entry and not new drawing code. ON by default (Cyrus 2026-10-02: wanted the layer back on every vertical).

Estimated positions from next-train ETAs, NOT GPS. `symbol: mtr-train` plus a per-feature `bearing` reuse the moving-layer icon-rotate path (overlays.ts pointLayer); the popup is the aircraft one so the shared builder already reads its fields. The layer animates: a requestAnimationFrame loop re-runs estimateMtrTrains with ttnt decremented by wall-clock, so trains slide smoothly along their line between the 30s schedule re-fetches instead of jumping each poll.

Reference geometry for the MTR: one LineString per heavy-rail line (plus the 落馬洲 / 康城 spurs), generated from data/mtr_stations.json by hand (see the file). `geom: line` draws through overlays.ts lineLayer with the official line colour carried per feature. OFF by default — it is a backdrop the reader turns on when they want to read the train layer against the network.

AIS vessel positions from VesselAPI, a twice-daily snapshot (not live — aisstream.io went silent 2026-08 and blocks datacenter egress). Same pointLayer path as aircraft: `symbol: vessel` plus a per-feature icon-rotate on `bearing` (COG, falling back to heading). OFF by default for the same reason aircraft is: a moving layer nobody asked for is a layer on every reader's map.
